results.name: Thirty rolling output updates after retention limit

implementation: Virtualized FileTree plus exact monotonic UTF-16 outputLength Terminal deltas; no overlap heuristic.
input: Synthetic 1,000/10,000 file metadata and 4,860,000-character compiler text rendered by actual production components with production React. No real project, model, command, or guest is controlled by the fixture.
method: CUA clicked benchmark controls. Fixture measured performance.now around flushSync and two requestAnimationFrames. Output completion checks read actual xterm accessibility markers. Keyboard and wheel observations below came from CUA input plus read-only DOM inspection.

keyboardObservations.note: Fixture menu callback records the actual target as selection; it does not render the workbench rename dialog.

keyboardObservations.action: Two-page wheel scroll upward while final file stays focused
keyboardObservations.note: Focused off-window row remains mounted while visible row window changes.

limitations: Single Chrome 153 desktop run; Safari and VoiceOver were not tested in this performance fixture.
Concurrent browser Linux npm installation was deliberately backgrounded by agreement during this short foreground test; this is not an idle-machine benchmark.

Baseline fixture Explorer used flex/overflow-hidden; final fixture uses block/overflow-auto matching the actual Explorer. Exact timing ratios should not be treated as a controlled benchmark; DOM counts and reset-vs-delta behavior remain directly observed.
Initial 10,000-file construction still recorded a 60 ms long task. Virtualization bounds DOM cost but does not eliminate model sorting cost.

Initial 500,000-character xterm accessibility-marker latency was 975.7 ms; this is not parser duration. Installed xterm 6 throttles screen-reader row refresh to once per second. Rolling updates had no recorded long tasks in this run, but final marker arrived 433.7 ms after the update loop.
The fixture does not include actual controller transport. Separate controller and delta tests cover monotonic counts and identical retained snapshots.
External selected-path updates keep the selected row mounted; automatic scrolling to external selection was not added. Keyboard End/Home explicitly reveals its focus target.
